correctness.rationale: Every linear isomorphism to the Euclidean plane pulls the Euclidean norm back to a positive-definite quadratic form. Averaging that form over the coordinate sign-change isometries preserves the same two-sided comparison with the Banaś--Frączek norm and eliminates the cross term, so the global optimization reduces without loss to \\(q_t=x_1^2+t x_2^2\\). The exact directional ratio \\(\\max\\{\\lambda^2,1+u\\}/(1+tu)\\) yields three exhaustive t-regimes whose minimum is \\(2-\\lambda^{-2}\\) at \\(t=\\lambda^{-2}\\). An explicit pair of unit vectors attains the same von Neumann--Jordan ratio, while the Euclidean parallelogram comparison supplies the matching upper bound. Quantifiers, boundaries, and the x_1=0 direction are included; no numerical experiment substitutes for proof.

value.rationale: The Banaś--Frączek plane is a named classical test family introduced to study deformation geometry and repeatedly revisited for exact Banach-space constants. Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance is the natural affine measure of how far this two-dimensional norm is from Hilbert geometry. The result gives the full parameter dependence, an explicit optimal ellipse, and an exact identity with a known Jordan--von Neumann constant, so it is a reusable structural fact about a standard family rather than an arbitrary slice or numerical recomputation.
